title: Integrated lunar transfer/landing, refueling and abort architecture audit for OTA-TEC-0092
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0092 early-phase combined lunar transfer/lander dossier. Focus only on the technical architecture dimension not already covered by the related CYGNUS, Starport Launcher, PELICAN and Gateway audits: (1) compare real and studied integrated versus staged lunar transfer/landing architectures and identify what mission functions can plausibly be combined in one vehicle; (2) assess orbital refueling / propellant-transfer constraints, rendezvous burden, cryogenic or other propellant-management implications and reliability effects for an early low-flight-rate architecture; (3) establish representative LEO-to-lunar-surface delta-v and mass-closure requirements sufficient to constrain, but not invent, vehicle mass, propellant type or tanker count; (4) assess plume-surface interaction, elevated/high-mounted engines and other landing-site mitigation approaches without asserting a fictional configuration; (5) assess abort, rescue, redundancy and common-mode-failure implications when transfer and landing functions are concentrated in one vehicle; (6) identify which findings can be inherited from existing 0082/0083/0084/0087 evidence and which are genuinely unique to an integrated vehicle; and (7) keep the 2040-2048 placement, Pioneer name, succession sequence and all canonical timeline choices explicitly [F/OFFEN]. Do NOT set tanker flights, fleet size, passenger count, turnaround, costs, unlocks or other NOXIA balancing values.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0092 is an uncovered mapped technical object created to close the early Moon-transport continuity gap. Its current dossier is explicitly ENTWURF/non-canonical until integrated-architecture, refueling, landing and abort constraints are source-pinned. Existing component/vehicle audits provide reusable evidence, so this job must synthesize rather than duplicate them.
real_world_anchor: Lunar transfer/lander mission architectures; orbital propellant transfer and rendezvous; lunar landing plume-surface interaction; abort and rescue architecture; rocket-equation/delta-v constraints.
novelty_reason: First exact-source audit of the integrated early lunar transfer-plus-landing system as a system architecture. It deliberately reuses existing vehicle/subsystem research instead of re-researching those objects independently.
